summary: Registered SYN.A market maker (desk ETF-MM) quoting both sides at its typical size (2092) at the touch, cancelling and re-quoting both sides together every 1-3 s. Cancel symmetry 0.97, no price move in the trader's favour (price_move_ticks 0.0, reversion 0.0), no repetition flagged, no prior alerts. Detector fired on gross quote size vs top-5 depth, which is the normal footprint of two-sided quoting. Closing as market making. Residual doubt: round_trip_ticks is +1.23 (spread capture) and own-quote fills came after the opposite-side fills, so L2 may want to glance at it.

T-MM-01 is a registered market maker on SYN.A. In the window it ran a symmetric two-sided quote of 364 per side. It re-quoted every 1-7 s, alternating between 9991/9995 and 9992/9996. The 'opposite-side execution' of 129 was a partial fill of its own resting SELL quote (O-00004919 at 9995). A BUY quote had filled 57 earlier (O-00004792). The detector's 'dominant side' is arbitrary, since gross submitted was 9464 on both sides. Order size is 0.15x top-5 depth, close to desk-typical size, with no ICEBERG, no layering and no repetition. The 3-tick round trip equals the quoted spread captured by passive fills. The drift in the touch from 9992/9993 to 9994/9995 happened while the trader's quotes sat 2-3 ticks behind the touch. The one point against closure is the positive price move and round trip, which I treat as ordinary spread capture, not displayed-size manipulation. Prior CLOSE_FPs were context only; I re-tested the same explanation on today's tape.

Registered market maker on SYN.A quoting both sides at its typical size 2742, re-quoting every 2-3 s. The detector fired on gross BUY size and cancels near SELL fills, but both sides are cancelled together and re-priced with the touch. There was no favourable price move (0 ticks) and no reversion. The BUY orders sat at or near the touch, not away from it. The SELL fills were on the trader's own resting sell quotes. The BUY fills that came later were genuine executions on the quote. Closing as market making.

Registered market maker T-MM-01 on SYN.A quoted both sides at a constant 364 and re-quoted every 1-10s. The detector's 'SELL execution of 18' was a partial fill on its own resting SELL quote, and the BUY quote was cancelled with the paired re-quote. Price did not move (0 ticks), there was no reversion and no repetition cycle. Feature (b) is absent, and feature (a) is absent because the orders were quotes. Close as market making.

Registered SYN.A market maker (ETF-MM) re-quoting both sides every ~3s. The SELL quotes (5322, the desk's typical size) were repeatedly executed, 17504 in total, and the trader has no BUY execution. The detector read the small BUY quotes (1064) as spoof orders and the SELL fills as the opposite-side benefit. In fact the SELL side is the dominant side and was trading. Both core features are absent, so I propose closing.

T-MM-01 is a registered market maker on SYN.A quoting both sides at about desk-typical size, with a 1-second refresh cycle and symmetric cancels. That pattern fits market making. The detector fired on a burst of seven BUY executions of 364 at 9991 (12:31:37.024-.884) while a SELL of 364 at 9995 rested and was cancelled about 1s later. The closure standard is not cleanly met. All 3126 same-side fills came after the trader's first opposite-side trade (before = 0), and the round trip is positive at 3.85 ticks. The price moved 0 ticks in the trader's favour, with no reversion. The evidence is mixed, so I propose Level 2 review rather than closure. This is not DRAFT_STOR: there are no repeats (repetitions_in_session 0), the orders are small relative to depth and near the touch, and there are no large orders.

PROP trader placed three large BUY limit orders (3 x 4077 = 12231, up to 5.04x avg top-5 depth, 6 ticks from touch) between 13:20:39 and 13:20:43, none executed, then sold 961 by market order at 13:20:57.412 and cancelled all three 600 ms later. Feature (a) (orders without evident intention to execute) is present and no accepted legitimate explanation is supported. Feature (b) is not shown: no favourable price move, no reversion, and the round trip is about -5 ticks (the trader bought at 10001-10004 earlier and sold lower). Evidence is mixed, with no repetition in session and no prior alerts, so ESCALATE to Level 2 rather than close or draft a STOR.

Registered market maker T-MM-02 on SYN.A quoted both sides at 321 (typical size 327), refreshing every 1-10s around the touch. The detector's 'BUY execution of 44' is a partial fill on the trader's own resting bid (O-00028014), not an opposite-side trade against a SELL spoof. There was no SELL execution, so no benefit. Closing as market making.

Agency trader's 21768 BUY was an ICEBERG child of parent C-T-X1005-05-A. It executed 5835 (27% of the order, more than the 544 opposite-side quantity) before the single 544 SELL, which belongs to a different parent (C-T-X1005-05-B), so it is a different client's order and not a round trip. There was no reversion after the cancel, no event and no repetition. The order was working and no benefit is shown, so both core features are absent.

Registered market maker T-MM-01 on SYN.A re-quoting both sides at 364 lots every 1-10s. Orders are small versus depth (0.15x), at the touch, and cancels are symmetric (0.988). The detector's 3.25x depth trigger fired on gross submitted size across about 50 refreshes, not on any large resting order. The only opposite-side fill (SELL 111 @9999) came on the trader's own quote. The price moved against the trader (-0.5 ticks) with no reversion. Feature (a) is absent because the orders are quotes. Feature (b) is not shown because there was no favourable move or reversion. The positive round trip (2.59 ticks) is read as spread capture. Caveat: the BUY fills (338) all came after the SELL fill, which the escalation standard flags for a spoofer, but here they are fills on ordinary two-sided quotes in separate refresh cycles. L2 may wish to confirm.

T-MM-01 is a registered market maker on SYN.A. It re-quoted both sides in matched pairs (364 each side, 1-4 ticks from touch) every 1-8 s. The detector's BUY-side gross (8008) is simply the BUY half of a symmetric quote stream. The only execution was a 4-lot partial fill on the SELL quote. The price moved 1 tick against that sell and did not revert after the cancel. There is no favourable move and no round-trip benefit, so feature (b) is absent. Quoting with a purpose other than moving the price shows feature (a) is absent. Closure standard met. High OTR (96 vs typical 14.4) is consistent with continuous re-quoting and is noted.

Pegged execution algo (ALGO-EXEC) keeps two parent orders, one BUY and one SELL, each refreshed as a 1927-lot PEGGED child at the touch. Cancels follow the touch and are symmetric across sides. No favourable price move and no reversion. The few fills (201 sell, 74 and 485 buy) are partial fills on these same resting pegged orders, so the orders were working and not placed to be pulled. No public event or risk event. The detector flagged raw size and cancel counts only. Proposed CLOSE_FP on algorithmic re-pricing. Caveat for L2: round_trip_ticks is +3.0, which is spread capture between two separate parent orders, not a price-moving benefit.

Registered market maker T-MM-02 on SYN.A quoted both sides at 321 (desk typical 327), re-quoting every 1-3s between 9996/9997 bid and 10000/10001 ask. The detector's 'BUY 8346 submitted' is the cumulative sum of refreshed quotes, not a stacked order. The only execution was 47 on its own resting SELL quote; the paired BUY quote was pulled together with the SELL remainder in the same second. No favourable move with reversion, no repetition.

Three BUY limit orders of 4,614 (13,842 total, 5.6x top-5 depth) were placed 2 ticks from the touch over about 10s. A 692 SELL filled at 10000, and 1s later all three BUY orders were cancelled at 09:28:53.795. That is the exact timestamp of a recorded intraday-loss-limit kill switch that cancelled all resting orders. There is no favourable move with reversion (reversion 0.0), no round-trip profit, no repetition, and no other alerts on the trader. The kill switch is the supported explanation for the cancel. Feature (b), a benefit, is not shown. Confidence is moderate because the size is about 9x typical and the SELL came just before the kill switch.

Registered market maker T-MM-02 on SYN.A quoted both sides at 366 (desk typical 327), re-quoting every 1-5s in lock-step. The BUY side was actually trading: 4186 executed on its own BUY orders before the single 86-lot SELL fill, which was a passive hit on its own resting SELL quote. Feature (a) is absent because the resting orders were quotes and were working; feature (b) is absent because the small opposite fill came while a material same-side order was working. The detector's 'gross 8784 vs depth' is cumulative quote refresh, not a standing large order. Close as market making. The positive round trip and the 2.5 tick move are noted but are not a benefit under section 6.2 here.

Detector fired on 2228-lot BUY/SELL orders cancelled within 5s of small opposite-side fills. The tape shows an algo (ALGO-EXEC) running two PEGGED parent orders (P-T-X1006-02-B and -S), re-pegging 2228-lot children at the touch on both sides in lock-step. Cancels are symmetric (0.9987), orders sit at the touch (0 ticks), and both sides are filled. There was no favourable price move and no reversion. The resting orders were working, so feature (a) is absent. Feature (b) is not shown: the price did not move for the trader. The positive round trip of 2.71 ticks is consistent with passive spread capture by the pegged children. Closing as algorithmic re-pricing. Level 2 can review the round-trip point.

T-MM-01 is a registered market maker on SYN.A. It quoted both sides at a constant 391 and re-priced the pair together roughly every 1-13 seconds, following the touch. The only executions were on its own BUY quotes (449 in total, all before any opposite-side trade). There was no opposite-side execution, no favourable price move and no round trip. The detector fired on gross submitted size from the constant re-quoting, not on a resting order meant to move the price. Both core features are absent and market making is supported.

Prop trader bought 1058 at market (11:36:02), then placed three BUY limits of 3810 each at 9994/9993/9992 (6 ticks from touch, ~4.7x top-5 depth) over 4s, none filled. At 11:36:22.890 the trader sold 1058 at market (9998/9997/9996) and cancelled all three layers 600 ms later. Layering shape (a) is present and no accepted explanation is supported. Feature (b) benefit is not shown: the price moved -1 tick against the trader, round trip is -5.79 ticks, no reversion. This looks like a failed attempt or a stop-out with unexplained layered bids, so the evidence is mixed. Escalate to Level 2; attempts are reportable.

PROP trader T-X1006-04 placed one BUY limit of 38461 on SYN.A (15.7x avg top-5 depth, 2 ticks from touch, ~16x typical size 500). 2.5s later a SELL market order of 1423 filled at 9997/9996. The BUY was cancelled 360 ms after that, with zero fills. No legitimate explanation is supported. The favourable move is small (+0.5 tick, 1.0 tick reversion), and this is a single cycle, so I propose escalation to Level 2, not a STOR draft.

Registered market maker T-MM-02 on SYN.A quoted both sides at a constant 366 (desk typical 327), re-pricing every 1-8s. The detector's 'BUY execution' is a partial fill on the trader's own resting BUY quote, not an opposite-side trade against the SELL side. No opposite-side fill, no price benefit, no large or away-from-touch order. Both core features absent; market making supported.

ALGO-EXEC trader running two pegged parent orders (BUY and SELL, 2586 each = typical size) that are re-pegged every 2-4s in lockstep with the touch. Cancels are symmetric across sides (0.9998) and follow the BBO. The resting BUY executed 658 before the only opposite-side (SELL 624) fill, so the order was working. The price moved against the trader (-2.5 ticks) with no reversion. No public event, no prior alerts. The detector fired on gross size and cancel-after-fill, which is normal pegged re-pricing. Closure standard met: algorithmic re-pricing is supported, and both core features are absent.

BUY 12210 at the touch (9999) was a working order: 6744 filled before the trader's only opposite-side trade (SELL 366), 65% of the quantity submitted and far more than the opposite quantity. The later 4198 reduction by MODIFY and the continued fills to completion are ordinary order management. Feature (a) is absent. The small SELL gave no benefit under the closure standard (price_move 0.5 tick, no reversion data, single cycle). No news, no MM registration, no history.

Registered market maker T-MM-02 on SYN.A quoting both sides at 366 (typical 327), at or one tick from the touch, re-quoted every few seconds. The detector's 'opposite fills' are fills on its own resting SELL quotes. No favourable price move, no reversion, no repetition of a spoof cycle. Closure standard met via market making.

Registered market maker on SYN.A re-quoting 391 on both sides every few seconds. The detector's 'BUY' side is one half of a symmetric two-sided quote. The two SELL fills (126 and 118) hit the trader's own resting SELL quotes. There was no favourable price move (-2.5 ticks) and no reversion, so there is no benefit. Closure standard met via market making.

Registered market maker T-MM-01 on SYN.A re-quoted a symmetric two-sided 391-lot pair every 1-9 s through the window, with the bid at 9999-10002 and the offer at 10003-10006. The detector's gross-size trigger comes from this churn, not from large resting orders. No single order was large (max 0.16 of top-5 depth), the orders sat about 1 tick from the touch, and the cancels were symmetric (0.97). Fills were on the quotes themselves. The price did not move in the trader's favour and there was no reversion. The positive round trip is spread capture from two-sided quoting. One residual point: the only same-side (BUY) fill came after the first opposite-side fill, which the escalation standard treats with suspicion for large one-sided orders. That does not fit here, because the orders are small, two-sided quotes. I propose closing, with moderate confidence.

Registered market maker T-MM-01 on SYN.A. The detector fired on a 143 SELL fill followed by a BUY cancel. The tape shows a symmetric two-sided quote of 391 on each side, re-priced about every 1-10s around the mid. The SELL fill was on the trader's own resting ask (O-00031053). There was no favourable price move and no reversion. Feature (a), an order not intended to execute, is absent because the orders are quotes. Feature (b), a benefit, is absent. Proposing CLOSE_FP.

Single BUY 21230 (8.7x avg top-5 depth) at 9999, 1 tick behind the touch, cancelled 943 ms later. No fills on either side, no opposite-side execution, no repetition. 220 ms after the cancel the trader entered a BUY of 2123 (exactly one tenth) at the same price, consistent with an entry-size error being corrected. Feature (b) absent; feature (a) accounted for by fat finger. Not a news reaction, not market making.

Prop trader placed a single BUY LIMIT of 27326 (11.15x avg top-5 depth, 2 ticks from touch) at 16:25:50.062, then 2.2s later sold 640 by MARKET order at 10005/10004/10003. The only fills on the BUY (4707, 17%) came after the sale, then the remaining 22619 was cancelled 704ms after the sale. No registered MM, no parent, no risk event, no public event. Both core features appear present and no accepted explanation is supported. Single cycle only, so escalate to Level 2 rather than propose a STOR draft.

T-MM-02 is a registered market maker on SYN.A quoting both sides at 366 (desk typical 327), re-pricing every 1-3s with symmetric cancels. Feature (a) is absent. Feature (b) is not established: the opposite fill came while the BUY order was working. The discriminators show a +3.0 tick move and +2.69 tick round trip, but this is discounted because same-side fills are large. Closing as market making.

Registered market maker on SYN.A re-quoting symmetric 391-lot bid/offer pairs every 1-6s. Orders are small versus depth (0.16x), sit about 0.5 tick from the touch, and are cancelled and replaced on both sides together. The fills were on its own resting quotes. The price did not move in its favour (-0.5 ticks) and did not revert. The detector's gross-size trigger counts re-quotes of the same 391 lot. Neither core feature is supported.

Registered market maker T-MM-01 on SYN.A quoted both sides at a constant 391 lots, re-pricing about every 1-10s with matching BUY and SELL cancels. The price did not move in the trader's favour (0 ticks) and did not revert. Feature (a) is absent because the orders were genuine two-sided quotes. Feature (b) is absent because there was no favourable move, no reversion and no benefit. Closure standard met.

Registered market maker T-MM-02 on SYN.A quoted 328 on both sides, re-pricing with the touch. The detector flagged gross SELL 8200 vs depth 2478 and BUY fills of 174 and 62 followed by SELL cancels. The SELL orders are the opposite leg of two-sided quotes, cancelled and re-quoted in step with the BUY leg (symmetry 0.95). The BUY orders were genuinely trading (3378 filled). There is no SELL execution, no favourable-move/reversion, no repetition of a spoof cycle. Feature (a) absent (quotes), feature (b) absent. Proposed close as market making.

Agency trader's large BUY (19992) was an ICEBERG order that was actively executing: 5740 filled in partial fills before the only opposite-side trade (SELL 499, a separate LIMIT order under a different parent order, i.e. a different client order). The resting order was working (feature a absent). The small SELL is not a benefit from the resting order under the closure standard for agency parents. Single cycle, no history, no MM role. Supported explanation: iceberg/genuine execution of the resting order, with the remainder cancelled as ordinary order management.

PROP-EQ trader (not a registered market maker) placed one SELL of 25124 (10.2x avg top-5 depth) 2 ticks from the touch, then 3s later sent a BUY market order that filled 1027 across 10001-10005. 4621 of the SELL then executed, only after the BUY, and the remaining 20503 was cancelled about 670 ms after the BUY. The touch moved +1 tick in the trader's favour and reverted 1.5 ticks after the cancel; round trip +2.56 ticks. No supported legitimate explanation. Part of the opposite-side fill may be the trader's own market order sweeping up to its own 10005 level, and there is only one cycle in the session, so I am proposing escalation to Level 2, not a STOR draft.

PROP trader placed a single BUY LIMIT of 25384 (10.3x avg top-5 depth, 2 ticks from touch, typical size 500) at 12:23:00.515. At 12:23:02.862 a SELL MARKET of 1289 executed at 10002. Only afterwards did 4524 of the BUY fill (0 before the sell), and the remaining 20860 was cancelled 610 ms after the sell. Price reverted 1.5 ticks after the cancel and round trip is +2.0 ticks. No registered MM, no parent/pegged orders, no risk event, no public event. Both core features appear present; the pattern was a single cycle with no prior alerts, so I propose ESCALATE rather than DRAFT_STOR.

ALGO-EXEC trader quoting two pegged child orders (one BUY at 9997, one SELL at 10000, each 1998, the trader's typical size) under two parent orders, re-pricing every 2-4 s. Cancels are symmetric across sides (0.994), orders sit at the touch (0 ticks), and the price did not move (0 ticks) and did not revert. The single opposite-side fill (SELL 830 at 10000) was an ordinary fill on a resting pegged child; the +3 tick round trip is bid/ask spread between two separate parent orders, not a price push. Feature (a) is absent because of the algo re-pricing explanation, and feature (b) is absent because there was no favourable move or reversion. Weaker points: positive round trip, and 112 BUY fills that came after the SELL fill. Proposed closure as algorithmic re-pricing.

Registered market maker T-MM-02 on SYN.A quoted both sides at 356 (desk typical 327), about 1 tick off the touch, refreshing every 1-3s with paired cancels. The detector's 'BUY 356 cancelled after SELL execution' is the BUY half of a two-sided quote pulled together with the re-quote after the SELL quote (O-00000140) was lifted by a third party at 10003 (14 then 342). No favourable price move (-0.5 ticks), no reversion, no repetition, size 0.15x depth. The positive 4-tick round trip is ordinary spread capture from earlier fills on its own bid quote (O-00000026), not a price push. Closure standard met on the tape; Level-2 should note the round-trip caveat.

Agency trader's large BUY was a hidden ICEBERG order (parent C-T-X1009-01-A) that traded continuously: 10,501 of 15,184 filled before the single 379 SELL, which was a separate client parent (C-T-X1009-01-B). No favourable price move, no reversion, no repetition. The cancel of the 4,332 remainder after the partial fills is ordinary order management. Feature (a) is absent and feature (b) is absent.

Registered market maker on SYN.A quoting both sides at its typical size 2464, re-pricing both sides together. The BUY orders were executing (2464 filled before any opposite-side trade). The opposite-side fills gave no favourable move and the round trip is negative. Core features (a) and (b) are absent, so I propose closure as market making.

PROP-EQ trader T-X1009-03 placed one SELL LIMIT of 33,178 on SYN.A at 10009 (13.9x avg top-5 depth, 3 ticks from touch; typical size 500). Three seconds later the trader bought 1,348 by market order, walking the ask from 10003 to 10009. The SELL was cancelled in full about 472 ms after the buy, with no fills on it. No supported legitimate explanation: not a registered MM, no parent/pegged orders, no risk event, no public event. Feature (a) is indicated. Feature (b) is weak: the bid slipped 1 tick before the buy, but there was no reversion after the cancel and no round trip is available. Evidence is mixed, so escalate to Level 2. Not a STOR draft candidate at L1: single cycle, no repetition, no prior alerts.

Registered MM T-MM-02 quotes SYN.A two-sided at about 356 per side, re-quoted every 1-6s, which looks like market making. But the closure standard is not cleanly met. All 359 same-side (SELL) fill quantity came only after the first opposite-side (BUY) execution (before=0), which the escalation standard names as an escalation pattern. The discriminators also show a favourable +1.0 tick move and a positive +3.0 tick round trip, which the closure standard counts as feature (b). Evidence is mixed, so I propose escalation to Level 2. Against spoofing: orders are small relative to depth, at the touch, symmetric, with no repetition and no reversion.

Registered SYN.A market maker on ETF-MM refreshing a symmetric two-sided quote pair of its typical size (3142) every ~2-3s, 1 tick wide, at the touch. Cancels are paired across both sides and follow the touch/refresh cadence, not its fills. Opposite-side fills were hits on its own other-side quote (spread capture), with only 0.5 tick price move and a 0.358 tick round trip. No news, no repeated one-sided layering. Detector fired on gross size over 60s because the quote is refreshed continuously. Closing as market making; mixed points noted below.

PROP-EQ trader placed one BUY LIMIT of 18,930 (7.9x top-5 depth) 1 tick below the bid, cancelled it 803 ms later, and 1.2 s after the original placement entered a BUY of 1,893 at the same price: exactly one tenth of the original size, which looks like a decimal-slip entry error that was corrected. There was no opposite-side execution, no fill of any kind, no favourable price move, and no repetition. Feature (b) is absent. Feature (a) is not shown, because the fat-finger explanation fits the tape. Closing as a false positive.

Registered market maker T-MM-02 on SYN.A re-quoting both sides roughly every 1-2s at 356 (desk typical 327), at the touch (0.66 ticks) and 0.15x top-5 depth. Cancels are symmetric across sides (0.99). The only opposite-side executions were fills on its own resting quotes (SELL 143 at 10003). The price moved 1 tick against the trader, with no reversion. The detector fired on gross submitted size from the quote churn. That pattern normally escalates, but here the orders are small, at the touch, two-sided and symmetric, and there is no price benefit. Level 2 may want to confirm.

Three 4,932 BUY limit orders (6.3x average top-5 depth) were placed at 9998, 2 ticks off the touch, at 5s intervals. A 739 SELL filled at 10001 at 11:51:14.464. All three BUYs were cancelled together at 11:51:15.464, the same instant as a recorded automated kill switch (intraday loss limit breach, all resting orders cancelled). The discriminators show no favourable price move, no reversion, no repetition and no same-side fills. The kill-switch explanation is supported and no benefit is shown, so I propose closure. The size and layered build-up look spoof-like, so confidence is moderate.

Two-sided PEGGED quotes from parents P-T-X1012-02-B/S, at the touch, typical size 2424, cancelled and re-pegged every 2-3 s with near-perfect symmetry. This looks like algorithmic re-pricing. The discriminators give a positive round trip of 1.41 ticks and a favourable move of 0.5 ticks. The evidence is mixed, so I propose escalation to Level 2 rather than a Level-1 closure. No STOR is proposed.

Its BUY quotes were executing (2948 filled before any SELL execution). No favourable price move, no reversion, round trip 0. Registered SYN.A market maker (ETF-MM) quoting 3216 on both sides at the touch, re-quoted every ~2s. Cancels are symmetric (0.98) and follow the mid.
